name: Oil (Brent)
summary: Brent near $95, below $100 on deal hopes, but Hormuz remains largely shut to shipping
state: Brent was about $94.6 late on 4 Nov, down about 18% in a week; it fell below $100 on 4 Nov for the first time since early October as US–Iran talks continued (Yahoo Finance; Gulf News). The price alone is in the Watch band, but Alert holds on the physical outage: Hormuz is still largely closed, and the IRGC said on 4 Nov that four tankers hit mines near the strait (Reuters via US News).
for_you: Fuel and transport costs stay exposed to Gulf supply news; price swings of several percent a day have been common since late October.
rubric_hit: Major physical supply outage > 2 mb/d (Hormuz largely shut) = Alert; Brent $94.6 alone is Watch
basis_detail: raised above the data floor on reported events

sources.title: Gulf News — Trump signals 'heavy hit' as tankers catch fire near Hormuz
US News/Reuters — Iran's IRGC says four tankers ablaze after hitting mines near Hormuz

why: Oil feeds inflation, transport and household budgets; price spikes have preceded most post-war recessions.
drivers: OPEC+ output, Middle East supply risk, sanctions, demand, inventories, shipping disruption.

rubric.alert: Brent > $110, or 1-month change > +30%, or a major physical supply outage (> 2 mb/d).
